title: The federal contractor defense in Boyle
shortTitle: The federal contractor defense in Boyle
summary: Boyle recognizes a defined defense to certain state design-defect claims when imposing liability would significantly conflict with federal procurement decisions. It is a specialized federal common-law doctrine.
notes: The defense does not establish general immunity for contractors or excuse all defects. The Court’s conditions and remand posture remain central.

sections.Meaning: Boyle recognizes a defined defense to certain state design-defect claims when imposing liability would significantly conflict with federal procurement decisions. It is a specialized federal common-law doctrine.
sections.How to work through the question: Examine government approval of reasonably precise specifications, conformity to those specifications, and disclosure of dangers known to the contractor but not the government. Explain the federal interest and actual conflict rather than relying simply on a government purchase.
